clue.text: Try to keep cool behind back of Chris Martin

indicators.note: behind places the cooling piece after the letter from Chris

parts.note: a pig will wallow in mud as its way of trying to keep cool, a cryptic definition of the verb

explanation.surface: Someone attempting to stay calm standing behind the Coldplay singer Chris Martin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chris Martin' reads as Coldplay's singer, but Martin alone is the definition and Chris only gives its last letter, S.
explanation.definitionFit: Martins and swallows are closely related birds of the same family, and the house martin is often loosely called one.

clue.text: Waste? Congress cut pay

indicators.note: cut means the word for congress loses its final letter

parts.note: congress in its old sense of sexual intercourse means sex
pay means wage

explanation.surface: A grumble that a legislature reducing salaries is a waste of effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Congress' looks like the US legislature, but it is sex, which 'cut' trims to SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewage is the waste matter carried away in drains, a specific example of waste.

clue.text: Paltrow's line difficult without former lover

indicators.note: without means the former lover is removed from the word for difficult

parts.note: difficult means exacting, demanding

explanation.definitionFit: Gwyneth Paltrow is a film actress, so her line of work is performing on screen.

clue.text: Cast agrees call to make epic

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' reads as the actors but is the anagram signal for AGREES and CALL together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something epic is vast in scope, built on a grand, sweeping scale.

clue.text: Goes quietly inside and cries

P, for piano, is the musical direction meaning quietly

explanation.surface: Someone retreats silently indoors and sobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes' is the nursery sense of going to the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: To weep is to shed tears, so cries and weeps are synonyms.

clue.text: Clocks up in charts

definitions.meaning: to clock up is to register or log a total, as a meter does
charts here are documented lists and logs kept as a history

explanation.surface: Something notches up entries in the music charts.
explanation.definitionFit: Clocking up a figure is registering it, and charts are logs kept for reference, both senses of the word.

clue.text: Course favourite getting special treatment

parts.note: Redcar is a racecourse in North Yorkshire
a favourite is a pet

explanation.surface: A racecourse favourite horse being given pampered handling.
explanation.walkthrough: REDCAR is a seaside town in north-east England with a horse-racing course.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolling out the red carpet means treating a visitor as a VIP, so the phrase stands for lavish welcome.

clue.text: Fix You, Coldplay's left on box

parts.note: U is text-speak for you
re means on or about, as in business letters

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix You' looks like a song title, but only 'Fix' defines; 'box' is surface dressing for the TV.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix an ailment or problem is to remedy it, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Lawyers reviewed piece dealing with talk, endlessly

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang to rabbit is to chatter; the comma hides that 'endlessly' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To rabbit on is British slang for chattering at tedious length without stopping.

clue.text: Pod in sea picked up; depth subject of investigation

indicators.note: picked up, as a microphone catches sound, means the word is heard and spelt by its sound

parts.note: sea sounds the same as the word for a bishop's diocese
a police inquiry deals with a case

explanation.surface: A pod is found at sea and the deep water is being investigated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' looks like finding something in the sea, but it is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pod is the husk that holds a plant's seeds, which is exactly a seed container.

clue.text: Game Paltrow's playing with heartless one

indicators.note: playing, in the sense of fooling about, signals that the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter, so this is the surname alone

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is taken out of the word one

explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless one' reads as an unkind person, but it is ONE losing its middle N, giving OE for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Water polo is a team ball sport played in a swimming pool, an example of a game.

clue.text: After splitting underpants, fit can be tolerated

parts.note: split the word underpants into under and pants; pants, slang for rubbish, then signals scrambling the letters of under
fit in the sense of capable means able

explanation.surface: Torn underwear that can still be worn is bearable.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'underpants' into UNDER and PANTS: 'pants' (British slang for rubbish) is the anagram signal working on UNDER, giving ENDUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something endurable can be borne or put up with, the same sense as tolerable.

clue.text: Sweet thing in red on picture

indicators.note: on joins the two pieces, the colour word coming first in the answer

parts.note: ginger describes red hair
a snap is a quick photograph

explanation.surface: A dear person shown wearing red in a photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet thing' looks like an endearment for a person; it is a biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A gingersnap is a crisp sugary biscuit, so it is literally a sweet thing to eat.

clue.text: Sad is Coldplay's album?

indicators.note: the possessive reads as has, saying the band's name and the words before it contain the answer

explanation.surface: Asking whether Coldplay's new album is a gloomy one.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface implies Coldplay's music is sad; the letters run across 'Sad is Coldplay'.
explanation.definitionFit: Albums are issued on discs, so the question mark marks a disc as a fair stand-in for an album.

clue.text: Old telly model's leads; archaic set without colour

indicators.note: set, as in arranged or put in order, signals a rearrangement of the letters
the leads of the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: An old television set from an archaic era showed only black and white.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' looks like the telly set; it is the anagram signal working on OTM and ARCHAIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Achromatic is the technical word for having no hue, like black-and-white images.

clue.text: Clear "conscious uncoupling" essentially is rubbish

indicators.note: rubbish as a verb, to trash, signals that these letters are jumbled
essentially points to the essence, the central letters of uncoupling

explanation.surface: A clear verdict that the phrase 'conscious uncoupling' is nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conscious uncoupling' was Paltrow's phrase for her split from Coldplay's Chris Martin. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something conspicuous is clearly visible and obvious, the sense of clear here.

clue.text: Upset, show went on — run breaking story

indicators.note: breaking means the run letter splits the reversed words
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so these words read from bottom to top

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical
went on, of a show running, means ran
r is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A show that went on despite upset, with a run interrupting the plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reverses EVITA RAN to NARATIVE, which the R breaks into.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative is an account of events, which is what a story is.

clue.text: In production, we uncovered Coldplay hit

indicators.note: in production means the letters are being made into something new, rearranged
uncovered means the band name loses its outer letters, its covers

explanation.surface: A Coldplay hit record that the band produced themselves, unveiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit' looks like a chart hit; it means struck. 'uncovered' strips Coldplay to OLDPLA.
explanation.definitionFit: To wallop is to strike hard, so walloped and hit are synonyms in the past tense.

clue.text: Stories and books

definitions.meaning: stories as in tellings or reports of events
books as in a firm's financial records

explanation.surface: Stories and books.
explanation.definitionFit: An account is a narrated report and also a ledger record, so plural tellings and plural ledgers share the word.

clue.text: Cycling race, clear to pedal

indicators.note: cycling, going round and round, signals that the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: In a cycle race, the way is open to pedal hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pedal' looks like a cyclist's verb, but it is a car's pedal.
explanation.definitionFit: The accelerator is the car's foot pedal that makes the engine go faster.

clue.text: Retract one's rings?

parts.note: to retract a decision is to cancel or annul it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Taking back one's engagement and wedding rings.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a broken engagement; 'one's' gives I plus a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Annuli is the Latin plural for ring-shaped figures, as in geometry or anatomy.

clue.text: Apple for one, hugging band's leader, lost voice

indicators.note: hugging means the tree word wraps around the other letters

parts.note: an apple is an example of a tree

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter

parts.note: l is the abbreviation for lost in sports results tables

explanation.surface: Apple, the label that signed the Beatles, embracing a band's frontman who has lost his voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apple' looks like the record label; it is an apple tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Treble is the highest singing voice, especially a boy soprano's.

clue.text: City big for country

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
OS stands for outsize, a clothing size meaning big

explanation.surface: A large city that stands in for a whole nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Laos is a landlocked nation in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Toilet is small for stars

parts.note: can is American slang for a toilet
small means minor

explanation.surface: A toilet that is too small for celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stars' reads as celebrities; it is a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Canis Minor, the Lesser Dog, is a constellation, a group of stars.

clue.text: Line that is to bag — let me see part of gut

indicators.note: to bag is to capture or enclose, so the letters for that is surround the line

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is
um is the hesitant noise of someone saying let me see

explanation.surface: A doctor muses over a line of diagnosis about some part of the gut.
explanation.definitionFit: The ileum is the final section of the small intestine, a portion of the gut.

clue.text: See 9
To pretend to sing on track for show

to mime is to mouth the words to a recording

explanation.walkthrough: PANTOMIME is the British family Christmas stage show, with songs, slapstick and audience shouting.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantomime is a theatrical entertainment, a kind of stage show.

clue.text: Change ending to hit, one's up for success?

parts.note: to thump is to hit

explanation.surface: A hit gets a new ending, and someone signals approval.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a raised one signals success, as in thumbs up.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbs-up gesture means approval or success, so the digit raised is the one up.

clue.text: Get shot of Sun model after turning over papers

indicators.note: after means the sun and model pieces follow the turned papers
turning over means the word for papers is read backwards

parts.note: ID, identity papers
s is the abbreviation for sun or Sunday
to pose is to model for an artist

explanation.surface: Getting rid of a Sun tabloid model after flicking through the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun' looks like the British tabloid, but it is just S.
explanation.definitionFit: To get shot of something is British slang for getting rid of it, which is what disposing of it means.

clue.text: Speed of sound: nothing going for current engine

o, the zero, means nothing
i is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.walkthrough: MACH ONE loses an O, and I comes in.
